column1: # Tall Tales Fishing: every fish, compiled by tools/fishing/fishing.py (art: tools/fishing/sprites.py).
# Tab separated; '#' lines are comments. One row per fish.
#   id          item id under villagefriends: (for 'existing' rows, the minecraft: item)
#   rarity      common uncommon rare epic legendary
#   water       where it lives, comma list: river lake swamp ocean warm cold deep cave deepcave, or any
#               (ocean = any ocean; warm/cold/deep = those oceans only; cave = underground water; deepcave = below y 0)
#   region      the land around the water, comma list: plains forest desert badlands savanna jungle swamp snowy
#               taiga mountain mushroom cherry, or any. Read from the biomes around the bobber, so a river
#               running through the desert is desert water.
#   time        any, or comma list of dawn day noon dusk night
#   weather     any clear rain thunder (rain includes thunder)
#   season      any, or comma list of spring summer autumn winter (only with Turning Seasons installed;
#               without it the fish bites all year)
#   size        length range in centimetres, min-max
#   behavior    how it fights in the catch-bar minigame: smooth mixed dart sinker floater
#   flags       comma list or -: existing (a vanilla item), shellfish, inedible, poison, notreat (pets refuse it)
# Legendary fish never stack, aren't food, and residents tell tall tales about where they bite.

column13: text
The old reliable of cold seas. Salted, it feeds whole villages through the winter.
Born in rivers, grown in the sea, and home again to spawn. Strong for its size.
Swells into a spiky ball when it's frightened. Don't eat it raw. Really, don't.
A flicker of colour from the warm reefs. Every one is painted a little differently.
Small, silver and everywhere. Every angler's first catch, and every heron's lunch.
A whiskered little bottom-feeder that bites at almost anything.
Red-eyed and bony. Old anglers say a roach can count your hooks.
Quick as a dart in clear, running water on bright days.
A greedy river fish with a mouth like a coin purse. Eats cherries that fall from the bank.
Striped and spiny-finned. Where there's one perch there are twenty.
A patient pond fish. Monks keep them in stew ponds for Fridays.
The doctor fish: folk say a sick fish rubs against a tench to be healed.
A round little sunfish that guards its nest in the shallows.
Pale and mild. Northern villages smoke it by the barrel.
Hardy enough to live in a puddle. Mothers carry their young in their mouths.
A little freshwater lobster that backs away under stones.
Born in the dark and never needed eyes. Feels its way along the cave floor.
Deep-bodied and slimy. Shoals of bream turn the evening water to bubbles.
The freshwater wolf. Waits in the weeds, then strikes like a thrown spear.
Spotted gold and red. Rises to a fly at first and last light.
A pink stripe down its side, like a rainbow caught in a stream.
Four whiskers and a stubborn pull. Hugs the gravel in fast water.
Wriggles across wet meadows on rainy nights. Nobody knows where they're born.
All mouth and appetite. Has been known to swallow a duckling.
Bronze and spirited. Leaps clean out of the water when hooked.
Lives in water so cold it aches. Its belly turns red as a winter sunset.
A jawless thing with a mouth full of rings of teeth. Kings once feasted on lamprey pie.
A tiny blue fish that survives where nothing should. Plays like a puppy in warm pools.
Teeth like a saw. Mind your fingers when you take the hook out.
An ancient swamp fish that can gulp air when the water goes stale.
A fish that walks on its fins and climbs roots to look around.
Hides under pebbles in underground streams and only comes out to eat.
Glassy eyes made for the dark. Hunts when the moon is up.
The lady of the stream, with a sail of a fin. Smells faintly of thyme.
Whiskers as long as your arm. Comes up to feed when rain muddies the water.
A carp the colour of a crown. Rises at dawn in still, clear water.
The only cod of fresh water. Spawns under the ice in the dead of winter.
Leaps from the water to snatch beetles off low branches.
A silver giant of the savanna rivers. Grows as big as a grown man.
Breathes air and shakes off hooks in storms. Swamp folk call it the snake that swims.
A long beak full of needles and scales like armour. Older than the swamp itself.
A minnow that shines like a lantern in the deep dark pools.
A jewel of a fish found only in desert pools. Blink and it's gone.
A great armoured fish with a snout like a shovel. Its eggs fetch a king's ransom.
So pale you can see its bones. Lives in the black water below the world.
Swims in shoals of thousands. Pickled, salted, smoked: herring keeps a coast alive.
A little oily silver fish, best packed tight and grilled on a fire.
Tiny, salty and strong-tasting. A spoonful flavours a whole pot.
Striped like the sea on a windy day. Fights hard for its size.
Cruises river mouths sipping at the mud. Notoriously fussy about bait.
A cold-water cod cousin that hunts in packs.
A silver-pink fish with a gold band between its eyes.
Scuttles sideways and pinches anything it doesn't like. That's most things.
See-through and twitchy. Comes up to the light at night.
Not a cucumber. Not quite a fish. Mostly a lump that sits on the sea bed.
A small cod with antifreeze in its blood, at home under the ice.
The wolf of the sea. Hunts the surf when the tide turns.
A dark thumbprint on each side, from a saint's hand, the fishwives say.
Lies flat in the sand with both eyes on one side, waiting.
Red as a rose and snappish with it. Bites best in a warm rain.
A huge grey eel that lives in shipwrecks. Strong enough to pull a man in.
A small spotted shark. Its skin is rough enough to sand wood.
Blue-black in the water, red in the pot. Mind both claws.
A rough grey shell with a soft heart. Now and then, a pearl.
A drifting moon of a jellyfish. Beautiful, and not for eating.
The great flatfish. A big one is heavier than the angler who lands it.
Built like a cannonball and faster than a horse. It'll take the line to the horizon.
Green and gold in the water, it flashes blue the moment it's caught.
All head and mouth, with a little lure on its brow. Delicious, if you can bear to look.
A mane of striped, venomous spines. Handle it like a hedgehog made of nettles.
Clever enough to unscrew a jar. Holds on to the sea bed with all eight arms.
Glides over the sand like a cloak in the wind. Keep clear of the tail.
Its bill is a real sword. It leaps, it spins, it will not give up.
A long blue shark that follows boats in rough weather.
Fishes for its supper with a glowing lure. Tonight you fished for it.
A catfish older than the village bell. The miller's grandfather swore it took his dog.
A fish of hammered gold that rises at noon in the desert pools when the sun is fiercest.
A silver giant that rules the savanna rivers. Lions are said to drink upstream of it.
A pike of living ice, seen through frozen lakes on still, starry winter nights.
A sturgeon so old that moss grows on its back. Moves up the taiga rivers in the autumn rains.
A great shark that hunts the open sea under thunderstorms. Sailors pray never to see its fin.
The light in the marsh that leads travellers astray is no spirit: it's the lure of this fish.
A blind white eel that glows blue in the black water at the bottom of the world.
A dragon of a fish with jade scales. Jungle folk say it leaps for the rain itself.
